issues.legal_issue: The term “premises” in the definition of a factory includes open land used for work.
material_facts: The salt works occupied a large, mostly open area, with only temporary shelters and a few pump platforms.
Workers carried out salt-making activities across the open area.
issues.conclusion: Open land may constitute “premises” for the purpose of the factory definition; the absence of substantial buildings did not exclude the salt works.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(m) of the Factories Act, 1948 uses “premises” in a generic sense that includes open land, land with buildings, or buildings alone. Sections 7, 85 and 93 provide internal support for that interpretation, and the Act’s worker-welfare purpose is consistent with it. The Court distinguished Kent v. Astley and Redgrave v. Lee, which concerned earlier statutory schemes, and noted support from the Factories Act, 1937.

predicates.open_worksite_used_for_production: The operator used an open area as a worksite for production activities.
predicates.workers_work_at_site: Workers carried out work at the open worksite.

issues.definition: When workers carry out production work at an open worksite, the open land can fall within the meaning of premises used for a factory.

issues.legal_issue: The conversion of sea water into salt through human work aided by natural forces is a manufacturing process.
material_facts: Workers admitted sea water into reservoirs, filled crystallising beds, monitored the brine, collected and graded salt crystals, and bagged the salt.
Gravity and solar energy assisted the process, but workers’ activities helped bring about the conversion.
Sea water entered the works as brine and left as salt, a marketable article.
issues.conclusion: The treatment and adaptation of sea water into salt was a manufacturing process.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(k) of the Factories Act, 1948 includes treating or adapting an article or substance with a view to its use, sale, transport, delivery or disposal. The Court relied on Sedgwick v. Watney, Combe, Reid & Co. Ltd., Grove v. Lloyds British Testing Co. Ltd., Kaye v. Burrows and Hines v. Eastern Counties Farmers’ Co-operative Association Ltd., and The State of Kerala v. V. M. Patel. It distinguished cases concerning mere sorting or work that did not adapt an article into a different marketable product.

predicates.human_work_changes_material_into_marketa: Workers perform activities that change an input material into a different product that can be sold.
predicates.natural_forces_assist_the_process: Natural forces assist the workers’ activities in bringing about the change.

issues.definition: When workers’ activities change material into a marketable product with natural forces assisting, the conversion is a manufacturing process.

issues.legal_issue: A salt works where the required number of workers carry out a manufacturing process is a factory, and operating it without the required licence supports conviction.
material_facts: The works employed 47 workers in activities that converted sea water into salt.
The works operated without a licence.
The appeal challenged a conviction for operating a factory without the required licence.
issues.conclusion: The salt works fell within the statutory definition of a factory, and the conviction for operating it without a licence was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(m) and 2(k) of the Factories Act, 1948 define a factory by reference to the premises, worker threshold and manufacturing process, and define the relevant manufacturing process to include treating or adapting material into a product. Section 6 and the applicable rule required the relevant licence, while section 92 provided for the offence. The Court applied its interpretation of “premises” and “manufacturing process” to the facts and dismissed the appeal.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_unlicensed_factory_conviction and worker_threshold_met and manufacturing_process_at_worksite and operation_without_required_licence

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_unlicensed_factory_: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction for operating a workplace without a required licence.
predicates.worker_threshold_met: The workplace employed enough workers to meet the applicable threshold for treatment as a factory.
predicates.manufacturing_process_at_worksite: Workers carried out a manufacturing process at the workplace.
predicates.operation_without_required_licence: The operator worked the workplace without obtaining the required licence.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal of this kind, when the worker threshold is met, a manufacturing process is carried out at the workplace, and the operator lacks the required licence, the conviction is upheld.
